questions.q: What does it mean if the Query Plan tool's lowest-cost candidate plan for a query is a TableScan rather than an Index-driven plan?
options: That query is not benefiting from selectivity the way the WHERE clause might suggest, and is effectively scanning a large portion of the table instead of using an index
The query will fail to execute entirely
The query is guaranteed to be fast regardless of table size
TableScan means the query is using a custom index instead of a standard index
questions.explain: A TableScan result means the optimizer chose not to use an index for that query, which directly signals a selectivity problem of the kind covered in Lesson 4, even if the WHERE clause looks reasonable at a glance.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of testing a suspected slow query in the Execute Anonymous window before changing production code?
options: It permanently increases the org's governor limits for that query
It lets you measure that one operation's cost in isolation, separate from whatever else might be running in the real transaction, without deploying anything
It automatically rewrites the query to be more selective
It bypasses governor limits entirely for testing purposes
questions.explain: Execute Anonymous runs a block of Apex immediately without any deployment, making it a fast way to isolate and test one specific hypothesis (like a single query's cost) separate from the full complexity of a real production transaction.

questions.q: What does the Developer Console Logs tab's Execution Overview show for a given debug log?
options: A list of every user who has ever viewed that specific record
The exact dollar cost of running that transaction on Salesforce's infrastructure
A prediction of how the transaction will perform after the next platform release
A visual timeline breaking down where the transaction's elapsed time went, across categories like Workflow, Apex, and Database
questions.explain: The Execution Overview is a visual breakdown of elapsed time by category (Apex, Workflow, Database, etc.), which answers where time actually went in a specific transaction using real measured data.

questions.q: In the suggested diagnostic sequence, why does capturing a debug log and checking the Execution Overview typically come before using Execute Anonymous to isolate a specific query?
options: Because Execute Anonymous cannot be used until a debug log already exists
Because the order doesn't matter and is purely a matter of personal preference
Because the Execution Overview helps identify which category (Apex, Workflow, Database) is actually dominating the elapsed time, which tells you what's worth isolating and testing in the first place
Because the Query Plan tool requires a debug log to already be open
questions.explain: The Execution Overview narrows down where the time is going before you spend effort isolating and testing a specific operation — testing the wrong hypothesis in Execute Anonymous wastes time if the real bottleneck is actually somewhere else entirely.

questions.q: How do the Query Plan tool, Execute Anonymous, and the Logs tab complement each other in a single diagnostic workflow?
options: The Logs tab's Execution Overview identifies which category dominates elapsed time, Execute Anonymous isolates and re-tests the specific operation involved, and the Query Plan tool confirms whether a SOQL selectivity problem specifically is the cause
They are three unrelated tools that are never used together on the same problem
All three tools do exactly the same thing and only one is needed at a time
The Query Plan tool must always be used first, before any log is captured
questions.explain: Each tool answers a different, sequential question: where did the time go (Execution Overview), what does that specific operation cost in isolation (Execute Anonymous), and is selectivity specifically the cause for a SOQL query (Query Plan) — used together they build a complete diagnosis.
